scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Dhimsa originated in the Koraput district of Odisha, India.
It is deeply rooted in the culture of the tribal communities living near the Araku Valley and Borra Caves.
Historically, the dance was performed by unmarried youth as a social activity.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Dhimsa is performed for various reasons: as a relaxation during work, during matrimonial alliances, and for religious worship.
It serves as a communal bond, with no discrimination regarding who can join.
The 'Boda Dhimsa' variant is specifically dedicated to the worship of village gods and goddesses.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in a chain formation, typically consisting of 15 to 20 women who link together to form circles.
The movement is dominated by synchronized footwork and hand gestures.
Dancers move in patterns that create smaller and larger circles.
Watch for Goddi Beta, Boda Dhimsa.

Formation: Chain formation moving in expanding and contracting circles.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is traditionally played by men using a specific set of tribal instruments.
These include the Dappu (a drum played with a short stick), the Tudumu, the Mori (a trumpet-like reed instrument), the Kiridi, and the Jodukommulu.
Listen for the Dappu, Tudumu, Mori, Kiridi.
The sound is dominated by the sharp, percussive strike of the Dappu drum and the high-pitched, melodic wail of the Mori reed instrument, creating a loud and energetic atmosphere.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear bright, colorful sarees in earthy tones such as green, red, and yellow, typically worn at calf-length (just below the knee) to facilitate movement.
They adorn themselves with traditional tribal ornaments and necklaces.
The dance is usually performed outdoors, in village squares or near natural sites like the Borra Caves and Araku Valley.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The sources do not name specific individual dancers or choreographers, as Dhimsa is a collective tribal tradition rather than a soloist-driven form.

There are twelve popular variations, including Bhag Dhimisa, Natikari Dhimsa, Kunda Dhimisa, Pathartola Dhimisa, Pedda Dhimisa, Sambor Nisani Dhimisa, Bayya Dhimisa, Mouli Dhimisa, Choti Dhimisa, Boda Dhimsa (ritual worship), and Goddi Beta Dimsa (forward and backward movement).
Dhimsa is a tribal folk dance of the Porja and other communities in the Odisha-Andhra Pradesh border region.

narration: The Boda Dhimsa variation involves the worship of village gods and goddesses; outsiders should observe with respect and follow local guidance regarding participation in ritual sequences.
